answer: The SAR backscatter analysis identifies a flooded region with 266 water pixels, representing 0.41% of the total area, based on a VV polarization threshold of -16.0 dB. The SDWI metric, though computed, was not used to generate the water mask. Optical methods highlight 10,770 water pixels (16.4% of the image), but there is only a 123-pixel intersection with the SAR mask, yielding an IoU of 0.011 — indicating poor agreement. The coregistration check shows a pixel shift of 23 px in x and -97 px in y, with a weak correlation peak, suggesting misalignment between optical and SAR data. The flooded area appears as a dark, coherent patch in the lower right quadrant, consistent with the SAR water mask’s spatial distribution.
